title: AgentMixer: Multi-Agent Correlated Policy Factorization
headline: Open finding: AgentMixer converges to an epsilon-approximate correlated equilibrium, with epsilon identified by the centralized policy's optimality gap in the proof.

work.title: AgentMixer: Multi-Agent Correlated Policy Factorization
work.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

claims.label: Theorem 2 approximate correlated equilibrium
claims.gist: AgentMixer converges to an epsilon-approximate correlated equilibrium, with epsilon identified by the centralized policy's optimality gap in the proof.
claims.statement: AgentMixer converges to an epsilon-approximate correlated equilibrium, with epsilon identified by the centralized policy's optimality gap in the proof.
conditions: Individual-Global-Consistency equates centralized and decentralized policy modes.
Centralized correlated and decentralized product execution use the paper's distinct operators.
claims.quantifiers: For the policy output generated under the stated AgentMixer/IGC construction.

result.summary: IGC controls modes rather than joint laws; an optimal correlated policy and same-marginal decentralized product have positive CE regret 2/25 while the proof-defined epsilon is zero.
result.witness: IGC controls modes rather than joint laws; an optimal correlated policy and same-marginal decentralized product have positive CE regret 2/25 while the proof-defined epsilon is zero.
result.argument: Mode-versus-law audit, same-marginal common-seed counterexample, full-support perturbation and convergence-proof review. Limits: Does not challenge empirical results, every trained policy, or all weaker approximate-equilibrium theorems.
not_claimed: An unrestricted existential epsilon reading is vacuous rather than directly contradicted.

vor_check.detail: Source verification is at the canonical partial level; the record does not overstate Version of Record verification.

evidence.detail: A fresh separate-session hostile validation supports the stated finding; its scope and limits are summarized above.

author_response.covers: One author agreed that IGC mode agreement alone does not control the stochastic joint law, confirmed the 2/25 regret example, and said non-vanishing stochastic execution requires a stronger distributional condition.
